clue.text: Confirm a man refusing strong drink is French

parts.note: a teetotaller, abbreviated TT, is someone who refuses alcohol
est is the French for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a teetotal man is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true, a synonym of confirm.

clue.text: Dread capture

explanation.surface: Someone fears being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehend once meant to fear or anticipate with dread, and also means to arrest or seize.

clue.text: A down-trodden machine-operator

parts.note: not an oppressed factory worker but a foot pedal literally pressed down to work a machine

explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot lever that drives a machine such as a sewing machine or lathe.

clue.text: I know the — names of beings animalculous" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: I know the — names of beings animalculous" (Gilbert)

parts.words: I know the — names of beings animalculous" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap from the Major-General's song in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the Major-General's song in The Pirates of Penzance runs 'I know the scientific names of beings animalculous'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word describes Latin classification names of tiny creatures in the Major-General's patter song.

clue.text: Loans saved, can rebuild

indicators.note: rebuild tells us the letters of the words saved and can are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Money that has been saved can be lent to rebuild something.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are sums paid ahead of time, in other words loans.

clue.text: 7 down having risen sped to work

indicators.note: to work tells us the letters of risen and sped are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone got up and hurried off to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is CHEMIST, a dispensing pharmacist; 'having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, so a dispenser is one.

clue.text: A little seal gains shelter among seaweed

indicators.note: a little says only a small part of the following words is used
shelter among says the answer lies tucked inside the words seal gains

explanation.surface: A small seal finds cover in the weed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'shelter among seaweed' is wrong: the answer means seaweed, and 'shelter among' tells us it is hidden in 'seAL GAins'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algae are simple water plants, and seaweeds are the large marine kind.

clue.text: Note deposited in a box for 5 down

indicators.note: deposited in tells us the note is put inside the box

parts.note: a chest is a box
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banknote is put into a strongbox for safekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist, who makes up prescriptions, is a dispensing chemist.

clue.text: Determined to get the money back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for money is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: notes are paper money

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to recover their cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Set on means resolved or intent upon.

clue.text: Man receiving royal letters and present

indicators.note: receiving tells us the word for man holds the royal letters

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A man gets letters from the Queen and a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means in attendance, as when answering a roll call.

clue.text: Before one's placed in the church it should be correct

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: placed in tells us one piece is set inside the letters for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
one is I, and one's is 'one is', giving I and S

explanation.surface: Something should be correct before it is installed in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': I (one) plus S, set inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and correct are synonyms for exact.

clue.text: The division set about the American detectives

indicators.note: about tells us the word set goes round the detectives

parts.note: taken as written
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: A police division puts together a case against American detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the parts something is divided into.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position when a tip gave offence

parts.note: a tip is an end, as of a finger
angered means gave offence to

explanation.surface: Someone was put on the spot when the size of their tip upset the waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'tip' looks like a gratuity but is an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger someone is to put them at risk, a difficult position.

clue.text: He has his pride!

parts.note: a group of these big cats is called a pride, so the male animal heads one rather than being vain

explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for these big cats, and the male leads it.

clue.text: Change of accent is appropriate

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of of accent is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Altering one's accent is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to seize property officially, to take it for oneself.

clue.text: Time for getting level

explanation.surface: A clock time for a man trying to level a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the late part of the day, a time; evening also means making level or equal.

clue.text: Coloured head's lack of experience

parts.note: green is a colour
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone with dyed hair is naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means being inexperienced or naive.

clue.text: Odd posture adopted by a man speechifying

indicators.note: odd tells us the word posture is rearranged into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A man making a speech strikes a strange pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' just links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouter is someone who talks at length, holding forth.

clue.text: Withdrew soldiers and discussed terms

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Troops pulled back and negotiated.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to fall back or pull out.

clue.text: Refuse in sink

explanation.surface: Rubbish has been left in the kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to say no politely, and also to fall or go down, as health sinks.

clue.text: Study article in vessel's hold

parts.note: to con is to study

indicators.note: in tells us the article goes inside the word for vessel

parts.note: a tin is a vessel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A survey of an item in a ship's cargo space.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain is to hold within.

clue.text: Make an image of Muse

explanation.surface: A request to create a picture of a goddess of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror makes an image when it throws light back; to reflect is also to ponder or think deeply.

clue.text: A drop in the ocean

parts.note: not a tiny amount but a falling of sea level as the tide goes out

explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the falling tide, when the sea level drops.

clue.text: Issue a description of them

parts.note: issue here means offspring, so the word for male children describes them

explanation.definitionFit: Issue in law and old usage means children or descendants, here the male offspring.

clue.text: Remained sound, being sober

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for remained is heard rather than seen

parts.note: stayed means remained

explanation.surface: Someone stayed healthy by staying off drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sedate and serious.

clue.text: Conclude gold and black may be approved of

parts.note: to end is to conclude
or is the heraldic name for gold
sable is the heraldic name for black

explanation.surface: Gold and black colours might win approval in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: OR and SABLE are heraldic terms for the tinctures gold and black.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsable means fit to be backed or supported, something that can win approval.

clue.text: Boatmen can get so upset about a river

indicators.note: about tells us the turned word goes round the other letters
upset in a down clue tells us the word so is turned upside down

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowers might capsize on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS, which goes 'about' A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are crew members who row, a sense of the word for the rowers themselves.

clue.text: European staff

explanation.surface: Workers from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole is a native of Poland in Europe; a pole is also a staff or long rod.

clue.text: Edible shellfish needs salt and nothing else

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
alone means with nothing else

explanation.surface: A shellfish to eat needs only salt for seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' links; 'salt' looks like seasoning but is a sailor (AB, able-bodied seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is a large sea snail eaten as a delicacy, also called ormer.

clue.text: One who faces the truth about a heel

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a ship lists when it heels over to one side

explanation.surface: A person admits the truth about a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist accepts things as they are, facing facts squarely.

clue.text: Member of the ballet company could be Sudanese

indicators.note: could be tells us the word Sudanese can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A Sudanese dancer might join the ballet troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, from the French.

clue.text: A story for example seen in advance

indicators.note: seen in tells us one piece is found inside the word for advance

parts.note: to lend is to advance money

explanation.surface: A tale is previewed before it is published.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale, a story handed down.
